Compare old/new zipped triples in native order; first unequal tuple sets same false and breaks, equal pairs increment prefix only. Length change alone leaves same false even if shared prefix equal.

Return whole old pair if bounded end <= dirty, irrespective of changed availability, OR old hit nonnull with hit timestamp strictly before dirty and matching old/current lower availability. Short-circuit order matters; bounded null hit retained.

Invoke inherited first-crossing with selected scan start and original end; write under original full query key with current FULL-window availability, not suffix availability. Preserve native strict direction and fallback; no arbitrary-edit equivalence proof.

Current key wins even if null; else reuse positive native prior ordinal at/before common-prefix count; else retain prior null only for actual old membership and same timestamp triples. No previous object retained as result.

Write match ordinal/null; nonnull returns pair with CURRENT reactions[ordinal-1], not the previous object. No new bounds or physical identity test.

Evaluate previous then current Blue key to form inherited-stop key; local key construction may raise before guard.

Reuse prior inherited stop including null if current formation passes settled reaction window and key exists; else base A16 (which can virtually dispatch A30). Always write current; no current lookup shortcut.
Pair trigger key evaluates both Blue keys and expiry, including null expiry.

Require nonnull expiry, current formation settled reaction window, then all nonnull expiry/previous formation/previous stop event/current stop event strictly settled; generator filters null events and all short-circuits. Compute confirmation via virtual A27 before looking up source; source key is trigger index and returned confirmation, not entire Reaction identity.

Require confirmation settled, indexed trigger main-open settled and prior source key; nullable source can be reused. Otherwise call A17, which queries confirmation again and may virtually use A30. Write current result; no current source membership lookup.

Look up only prior zones. Null/missing allocates via A21; assign selected same-object or new record to current key then return. Current key is not consulted on repeated calls; key hash/type/construction/assignment errors propagate.
Separate continuation wrapper class describes replay from first mutable main with revised upstream inputs; no cache or publication occurs at class declaration.

Store direction; construct fresh live detector with null previous and dirty; detect before assigning result then detector on the new wrapper. Constructor failures do not produce a successfully constructed wrapper.
Result property returns new list of retained records, not deep copies; physical zone references retained. Copy allocation failure propagates.
Capture old detector; validate exact timeframe equality first; mismatch raises before dirty-index gate or new detector construction.
Inclusive dirty-index admission from zero to min(old candle count,new candle count). No exact-int validator; native comparisons and subsequent indexing govern failure.

Minimum available old/new main open at dirty position; each time array tested independently. Default is new last timestamp plus timeframe or null for empty new times; default evaluated eagerly before min consumes candidates. No implicit index clamp or normalization.

Construct candidate detector with retained direction, revised inputs, old detector and computed dirty time; perform detection before replacing wrapper fields. No explicit catch; external provider/input aliases are not transactional.

Replace candidate prior-history reference with fresh history before tuple assignment publishes candidate detector and result to wrapper. Prior/current history release is reference replacement, not a deep rollback of shared external state.

Return result property (fresh shallow list) after wrapper publication. Post-publication copy failure does not roll back; a pre-publication detection failure retains old wrapper fields but does not guarantee external alias rollback.
